beats.vo: Hey champ, welcome back! Ready for something really cool today?
beats.caption: Welcome back, champ!

beats.vo: Last time, we found out how apps work. Input, process, output. You give it something, it works, and it gives something back.
beats.caption: Last time: Input → Process → Output

beats.vo: Today is chapter three of Computers in Our World. It's all about robots, and automation!
beats.caption: Chapter 3 · Robots & Automation

beats.vo: Automation. Hmm, another big word! Don't worry. By the end of today, you'll be explaining it to your friends.
beats.caption: Au · to · ma · tion. Another big word!

beats.vo: Picture this. Your family goes to a new restaurant in the city. And guess who brings the food? A robot waiter! Let's call her, Bolt.
beats.caption: Meet Bolt, the robot waiter!

beats.vo: Bolt rolls up to your table, and hands you a plate of hot, crispy dosa. Then she rolls right back to the kitchen. Wow!
beats.caption: Bolt brings your dosa, then rolls back

beats.vo: Your little brother whispers, is Bolt happy to see us? Does she like her job? Hmm. What do you think?
beats.caption: Is Bolt happy? Does she like her job?

beats.vo: Here's the surprising truth. Bolt doesn't feel happy, or sad, or bored. That smiley face on her screen is just a picture. Someone put it there.
beats.caption: Bolt doesn't feel. The smile is just a picture.

beats.vo: So what is a robot, really? A robot is a machine that does jobs, by following instructions written by people.
beats.caption: Robot = a machine that follows instructions

beats.vo: And step-by-step instructions have a name you already know. An algorithm! It's the robot's recipe. Bolt's algorithm says, go to the table. Give the plate. Come back.
beats.caption: Bolt's algorithm: Go · Give the plate · Come back

beats.vo: Someone wrote those steps for Bolt. Without them, she'd just stand there, blinking. Remember Robo, who didn't know how to get water? Same thing!
beats.caption: No steps? The robot doesn't know what to do

beats.vo: Now, what about automation? Automation means letting a machine do a job by itself, again and again, without a person doing each step.
beats.caption: Automation: a machine does a job by itself

beats.vo: Have you seen a robot vacuum? It cleans the floor, row by row. Go forward, and turn. Go forward, and turn. Again and again, until the whole room is clean.
beats.caption: Forward, turn. Forward, turn. Again and again!

beats.vo: Doing the same steps again and again is called a loop. And robots love loops! They never get tired of doing the same thing.
beats.caption: Repeating the same steps = a LOOP

beats.vo: So the vacuum's whole algorithm can be tiny. Repeat. Go forward. Turn. Keep repeating, until the room is clean. Short, clear, and it works!
beats.caption: Repeat: forward, turn… until clean

beats.vo: Now picture a big car factory. A robot arm fixes the same part, on every single car. Car after car, all day long.
beats.caption: A factory arm fixes the same part on every car

beats.vo: Other robot arms pack boxes. Pick up a box. Put it on the belt. Pick up the next box. Same steps, every single time. That's automation!
beats.caption: Pick up box, put on belt… again and again

beats.vo: Would you get bored doing that a thousand times? I would! But the robot doesn't mind at all. That's why robots are great at repeat jobs.
beats.caption: Robots are great at repeat jobs!

beats.vo: But robots have a weak spot too. Let's go back to Bolt. Oh no! Your little brother knocks over his mango juice. Splash! It's all over the floor.
beats.caption: Oh no! Juice spilled on the floor!

beats.vo: What do you think Bolt will do? Clean it up? Call for help? Think about it.
beats.caption: What will Bolt do? Think!

beats.vo: Bolt just keeps following her steps. Go to the table. Give the plate. Come back. A spill isn't in her instructions, so she does nothing about it.
beats.caption: Bolt just keeps following her steps

beats.vo: A person would grab a cloth right away! People are much better at brand-new, messy problems. Robots are poor at them, unless someone gives them steps.
beats.caption: New, messy jobs? People do better!

beats.vo: Let's play a game. Robot can, or robot can't! Here are four jobs.
beats.caption: Game: Robot CAN or robot CAN'T?

beats.vo: Pack the same box, five hundred times. Invent a brand-new game. Sweep the floor every day. Comfort a sad friend. Which ones can a robot do? Pause, and think.
beats.caption: Which jobs can a robot do?

beats.vo: Packing boxes, and sweeping every day? Robot can! Those are repeat jobs with clear steps. Inventing a game, and comforting a friend? Robot can't. Those need new ideas, and feelings.
beats.caption: Repeat jobs: CAN. Ideas & feelings: CAN'T

beats.vo: Robots come in all shapes and sizes. There's the home robot, like a vacuum that sweeps your room.
beats.caption: Home robot: sweeps your room

beats.vo: The factory robot, like a robot arm that builds cars, or packs boxes.
beats.caption: Factory robot: builds cars, packs boxes

beats.vo: And the space robot, like a rover driving on Mars, taking photos of the red rocks!
beats.caption: Space robot: a rover on Mars

beats.vo: Different jobs, but the same big idea. Every one of them follows instructions, written by people.
beats.caption: Same idea: they all follow instructions

beats.vo: One more! Let's finish a robot's algorithm to water a plant. One, pick up the can. Two, walk to the plant. Three, hmm, something's missing. Four, walk back. So, what's step three?
beats.caption: Pick up can → Walk → ??? → Walk back

beats.vo: Tip the can, to pour the water! Without that step, the plant would stay thirsty.
beats.caption: Step 3: tip the can to pour water!

beats.vo: Okay champ, it's practice check time, just like the quiz.
beats.caption: Your turn: practice check

beats.vo: Why can't a vacuum robot invent a new game by itself? Pause the video, and think. Or write your answer on paper.
beats.caption: Why can't a vacuum robot invent a new game?

beats.vo: Here's one answer. It only follows the steps that people gave it. Nobody gave it steps for making a new game, and it can't think up new ideas by itself. Great thinking!
beats.caption: It only follows steps. No steps for new games!

beats.vo: Let's remember. Robots follow algorithms, steps written by people. They don't have feelings.
beats.caption: Robots follow algorithms. They don't feel.

beats.vo: They're great at repeat jobs. Hello, loops!
beats.caption: Great at repeat jobs: loops!

beats.vo: But they're poor at brand-new, messy jobs, without instructions.
beats.caption: Poor at new, messy jobs without steps

beats.vo: And home, factory, and space robots? Same idea, different jobs.
beats.caption: Home · Factory · Space: same idea

beats.vo: Chapter three, done! Now you know what robots can, and can't do, champ.
beats.caption: Chapter 3 done!

beats.vo: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
beats.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
